convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in MT5 indicators (iFractals, iForce) with standard parameters. Simple crossover entry/exit rules. Fixed lot position sizing. No external .mqh libraries for trading logic. No complex money management or multi-timeframe logic.

derived_values.name: Upper fractal level - the High price of the bar where an upper fractal was detected
derived_values.formula: iHigh(_Symbol, _Period, bar_index) where iFractals returns upper fractal at bar_index
derived_values.used_by: Long entry breakout condition and short stop-loss placement

derived_values.name: Lower fractal level - the Low price of the bar where a lower fractal was detected
derived_values.formula: iLow(_Symbol, _Period, bar_index) where iFractals returns lower fractal at bar_index
derived_values.used_by: Short entry breakout condition and long stop-loss placement

params.description: TP set as StopLevel multiplier applied to SL distance, or fixed via TakeProfit input param in points with digit adjustment

other_exits: Opposite signal closes current position before opening new one in reverse direction

custom_logic_notes: EA uses fractal breakout combined with Force Index momentum confirmation. Upper/lower fractal levels are dynamically found by scanning recent bars. SL is placed at the opposite fractal level. The Force Index crossing zero confirms momentum direction change. Digit adjustment is applied to SL/TP input values: if _Digits==3 or _Digits==5, values are multiplied by 10 to convert from pips to points. The EA scans backward from bar 2 to find the most recent confirmed fractal for SL placement and breakout level detection. Opposite positions are closed before opening a new trade in the reverse direction.
python_conversion_notes: Fractal detection requires scanning bars backward to find the first bar where iFractals returns a non-zero value for upper/lower fractal. This is a multi-bar lookback pattern not available as a simple indicator call in most Python backtesting frameworks - will need custom fractal detection function. Force Index is available in most libraries (e.g., ta-lib as FORCE_INDEX). Digit adjustment logic for SL/TP must be preserved: if symbol has 3 or 5 decimal places, multiply pip-based inputs by 10. Position management requires checking for existing opposite-side positions and closing them before entry. The new-bar guard means signals are evaluated once per completed bar.
